children: Ride-hailing company Uber Technologies and Chinese autonomous-driving company Momenta have begun trial operations for robotaxi services in Munich, bringing the companies closer to officially launching their services in Germany.

Momenta said Wednesday that it is offering free robotaxi rides for users who sign up for the pilot program on the Uber app in Germany. During the trial phase, a safety operator will be present in the car.
The initial stage of trial operations will cover most areas in northern Munich, it said on WeChat.
Germany is one of the hardest European markets to crack for robotaxi players, given its strict compliance and safety requirements.
Momenta operates a robotaxi service in Shanghai and has provided its autonomous-driving technology to major automakers including German brands such as Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Audi.
Uber has been collaborating with robotaxi companies to explore autonomous-driving services. The ride-hailing app has partnered with Chinese robotaxi companies WeRide and Pony AI in the Middle East.
